edits.old:
spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: nginx:1.27.1
edits.new:
spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      securityContext:
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: nginx:1.27.1
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
edits.why: Disable SA token automount, set RuntimeDefault seccomp, block privilege escalation. None of these should affect stock nginx.

skipped.reason: CPU limits need real usage data; a guessed value could throttle the app.
Memory limits need real usage data; a guessed value could cause OOM kills.
nginx writes to /var/cache/nginx and /var/run. A read-only root filesystem needs emptyDir mounts for these, and I can't confirm that without knowing what the app writes.
Stock nginx:1.27.1 runs as root. runAsNonRoot would stop it starting, and the image can't be changed.
Same as C-0013. It needs a non-root image, or a valid UID that has been tested.
Partly covered by the seccomp and privilege-escalation settings. A full non-root context would break stock nginx.
Dropping all capabilities would break root nginx, which needs CHOWN, SETUID and SETGID. That needs testing.
This needs a separate NetworkPolicy resource, and the right rules depend on traffic that isn't known. It is outside this file's edit scope.
